                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Documentation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2024-11-06, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/27.1/api/analytics-query-suggestions.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Search analytics feature needs to be explicitly enabled via the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`--enable-search-analytics` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`--analytics-dir`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'flags for query suggestions and other analytics features to work.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'--analytics-dir=/path/to/analytics-data \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'set\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's first create a new collection to which search queries will be aggregated and logged to.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`popular_queries` analytics rule that stores the most frequently occurring search queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'in the collection we created above.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you wish to send the search queries as events via the API, you can create an analytics rule that defines a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`search`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'event for consumption.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By setting\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`enable_auto_aggregation` to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`false`, only the search queries sent via the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'API will be aggregated.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"params": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"source": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"collections": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"products"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"name": "products_search_event"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With this rule in place, you can now directly send the queries as\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Search Analytics - Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-02-11, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/search-analytics.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Given that you need the context of user-behavioral data to get a complete picture of how your search experience is performing,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**we highly recommend instrumenting your search experience on the client-side**, to send additional search data along with the rest of the data you are already capturing, to your existing analytics platform.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As of v0.25.0, Typesense supports the ability to capture Search Analytics (the top searched terms) natively.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once the search terms are collected, you can then sort by the count of each search term to get the top search terms.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you are using the InstantSearch UI Library, it comes with out-of-the-box widgets to help you capture search data, and send it to your analytics tool of choice on the client-side:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'See the Linux Commit Search reference implementation for an example of how to implement this in code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'd typically want to listen to changes to your search field (with a debounce of say 1s), then capture the search term and search results displayed, and make an API call to your analytics platform using their API library, indicating that a search event has occurred."[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Collections API\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-04-08, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In Typesense, every record you index is called a `Document` and a group of documents with similar fields is called a `Collection`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Before we can add documents to Typesense, we need to first create a `Collection` - we give it a name and describe the fields that will be indexed from our `Documents`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are two ways to specify a schema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Pre-define all the fields to be indexed from your documents OR\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Have Typesense automatically detect your fields and data types based on the documents you index.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`POST ${TYPESENSE_HOST}/collections`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl -k "http://localhost:8108/collections?src_name=existing_coll" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-H "X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY: ${TYPESENSE_API_KEY}" -d \'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "new_coll"\n'[39m +
                      [32m"}'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8108/collections?src_name=source_collection&copy_documents=true' \\\n"[39m +
                      [32m"-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Retrieve the details of a collection, given its name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Definition** `GET ${TYPESENSE_HOST}/collections/:collection`'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'This section of the documentation details all the API Endpoints available in Typesense and all the parameters you can use with them.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Analytics - Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-04-17, last updated: 2026-04-18, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.1/api/analytics-query-suggestions.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `popular_queries`: Aggregate the most frequently occurring queries into a destination collection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'in the collection we created above.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We limit the popular queries to the top 1000 queries via the `limit` parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'First, create a collection to store the queries with meta fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The schema should include fields for the meta data you want to track:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "top_queries",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ "name": "q", "type": "string" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ "name": "filter_by", "type": "string" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ "name": "analytics_tag", "type": "string" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ "name": "count", "type": "int32" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then, create an analytics rule that specifies which meta fields to track:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "top_search_queries",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "popular_queries",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"collection": "hnstories",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"event_type": "search",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"params": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"limit": 100,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"expand_query": true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"meta_fields": ["analytics_tag", "filter_by"],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"destination_collection": "top_queries"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# typesense_analytics_rule | Resources | Fluent-Health/typesense ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-16, last updated: 2026-07-27, [Read more](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/Fluent-Health/typesense/latest/docs/resources/analytics_rule)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resource "typesense_analytics_rule" "popular" {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name = "popular_queries_rule"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type = "popular_queries"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'collection = typesense_collection.products.name\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Required\n'[39m +

                      [32m'### Optional\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `params` (Attributes) (see below for nested schema)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- `destination_collection` (String) Destination collection where aggregated rows are written.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://truespar.com/torque/docs/v1/analytics)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Analytics rules capture what your users search for - popular queries, queries with no results, per-document counters, and raw event logs - and aggregate them into collections you can search and facet like any other data.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Search Analytics | Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-02-11, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/search-analytics.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is data you are most likely already capturing in your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Given that you need the context of user-behavioral data to get a complete picture of how your search experience is performing,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**we highly recommend instrumenting your search experience on the client-side**, to send additional search data along with the rest of the data you are already capturing, to your existing analytics platform.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As of v0.25.0, Typesense supports the ability to capture Search Analytics (the top searched terms) natively.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once the search terms are collected, you can then sort by the count of each search term to get the top search terms.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you are using the InstantSearch UI Library, it comes with out-of-the-box widgets to help you capture search data, and send it to your analytics tool of choice on the client-side:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'See the Linux Commit Search reference implementation for an example of how to implement this in code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'd typically want to listen to changes to your search field (with a debounce of say 1s), then capture the search term and search results displayed, and make an API call to your analytics platform using their API library, indicating that a search event has occurred."[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Add metadata support to no_hits_queries · Issue #1971 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-26, last updated: 2024-11-27, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/1971)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example curl command:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl -k "http://localhost:8108/analytics/rules" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-X POST \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-H "X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY: ${TYPESENSE_API_KEY}" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m"-d '{\n"[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "product_no_hits",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "nohits_queries",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"params": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"source": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"collections": ["collection_1", "collection_2"]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"destination": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"collection": "no_hits_queries"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"limit": 1000\n'[39m +
                      [32m"}'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The no_hits_queries collection should log no-hit search queries along with the collection name (or some identifier) indicating which collection the query was executed against.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The no_hits_queries collection logs the queries but does not include the collection name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The workaround for now is to create a separate analytics rule for each no_hits rule and set a different source collection and destination collection in each.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`no_hits_queries`collection to aggregate no-hit search queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`collection_1`and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`collection_2`that return no results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`no_hits_queries`collection for logged queries.'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Typesense Analytics Rules Api | APIs.io APIs\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Create and manage analytics rules that control how search queries and user events are aggregated for query suggestions and relevance tuning.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search Ranking and Relevance | Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/ranking-and-relevance.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Handling No Results\n'[39m +
                      [32m`In some use-cases, if all of the user's search terms don't match any of the documents, you might not want to show the user a "No results found" message.\n`[39m +
                      [32m"In such cases, you can have Typesense automatically drop words / tokens from the user's search query, one at a time and repeat the search to show results that are close to the user's original query.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This behavior is controlled by the `drop_tokens_threshold` search parameter, which has a default value of `1`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This means that if a search query only returns 1 or 0 results, Typesense will start dropping search keywords and repeat the search until at least 1 result is found.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To turn this behavior off, set `drop_tokens_threshold=0`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search FAQs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/faqs.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. By default, when no results are found for a multi-keyword search query, then Typesense will start dropping words in the query one at a time, and repeat the search until enough results are found.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The definition of "enough" above can be configured using the `drop_tokens_threshold` search parameter and the direction of the dropping (left to right vs right to left) can be configured using the `drop_tokens_mode` parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You want to set `drop_tokens_threshold: 0` as a search parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With the feature explained above, if you set `drop_tokens_threshold: 0`, that disables the feature and Typesense will only return records where ALL the search terms mentioned in the query are present in the same record.'[39m
                  }
                ]
              },

                      [32m'The `q` and `count` fields are mandatory.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'We can now create a `popular_queries` analytics rule that stores the most frequently occurring search queries\n'[39m +

                      [32m"That's it!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The schema should include fields for the meta data you want to track:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +

            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +

            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
